subject: Request: Tiered rebate & one-time volume carveout for CardioSurge pilot — VP/CFO signoff
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena@cardiosurge.health>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: 2028-06-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot pricing ask (CardioSurge)

Vivek — thanks again for the demo yesterday. Quick follow-up from procurement: CardioSurge is willing to run a 6-month pilot but we need a steep unit discount for the first 3 months (roughly 60% off list) and a one-time volume credit to offset migration costs.

We can commit to a six-figure minimum spend across the pilot if we get the structure. Also need VPC deployment + SOC2 evidence (you flagged available). Can your team confirm if this is doable and who I should coordinate with for approvals?

Best,
Elena
Procurement Manager
CardioSurge

Attachments: initial-term-summary.xlsx (see attached usage assumptions)

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com, alex_martinez@redwood.com
Cc: 
Date: 2028-06-14T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Pilot pricing ask (CardioSurge) — recommendation + ask for VP/CFO clearance

Team — forwarding CardioSurge request. TL;DR: 6-month pilot, asking for 60% off for first 3 months + one-time migration credit (they propose $75k). They will commit to a minimum pilot spend (we think ~$250k gross). CardioSurge is strategic in cardiac device analytics — high technical fit and strong expansion potential across US hospitals.

Proposal I recommend: 40% off list for months 1-3 with a $50k one-time onboarding credit, plus a conditional step-back to our standard pilot rates for months 4-6. In exchange: 12-month renewal option at a preferred committed rate if they convert within 30 days of pilot end, and a 30% uplift revenue share clause if usage exceeds projections.

Why this structure: protects unit economics vs their ask, gives the customer headline price to close pilot, and creates clear conversion incentives. This will require VP/CFO signoff for any onboarding credits > $25k or effective blended discount > 50% over pilot. Seeking quick decision — procurement is pushing to sign before month end.

Attachments: Q3_usage_projection_cardiosurge.xlsx (their numbers), draft term pointers below.

Next steps I propose: Kim — can you run a brief unit-econ delta and signoff threshold? Marissa — if you endorse, can you escalate to the VP for commercial clearance? Alex — please prepare counter-term language for HubSpot/DocuSign. I can join a call with Elena if helpful.

— Vivek
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
vivk_kulkarni@redwood.com
(Attachment: cardiosurge_term_sheet_v2.pdf)

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2028-06-15T08:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pilot pricing ask (CardioSurge) — unit econ analysis

Vivek — ran the simulation on conservative usage. If we give 60% off for 3 months + $75k credit we end up with negative contribution margin in month 1 and marginal breakeven by month 4 assuming they hit projected scale. My preference is Kim’s suggested structure (your 40% + $50k credit) or we make the $50k credit conditional (payable as rebate on achieved usage thresholds).

Questions for clarity before VP/CFO:
 - Are the VPC setup and initial infra costs billable to the customer or included in the credit?
 - Can we build a clawback clause if they terminate before conversion?

If we keep the one-time credit <= $50k and structure as performance rebate, I can sign off and recommend VP approval for the blended discount to not exceed 48% effective over the pilot term. Anything beyond that needs CFO signoff and a formal memo.

Kim
Head of Revenue Finance
Redwood Inference

On Jun 14, 2028, Vivek wrote:
> Team — forwarding CardioSurge request...

From: alex_martinez@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: 2028-06-16T10:11:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pilot pricing ask (CardioSurge) — commercial mitigations

Echoing Kim — we should move the majority of the concession into an outcome-based rebate. I suggest: 35% up front discount (months 1-3), $50k onboarding credit paid as a rebate once month-3 usage >= 80% of projected, and a 12-month renewal commitment clause with a 6-month lookback true-up. Also propose a 90-day tech validation clause: if they hit <50% of targets by day 90, credit clawback triggers and contract rolls to full list.

I can lock the customer on those terms today if finance approves the $50k rebate structure. This protects us and keeps the anchor price lower for CardioSurge.

— Alex
Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, alex_martinez@redwood.com
Date: 2028-06-18T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pilot pricing ask (CardioSurge) — recommend exec clearance memo

Vivek/Alex/Kim — I support the outcome-rebate approach Alex outlined. CardioSurge is a high-velocity logo with strong referral potential across hospital systems; accepting a measured concession improves conversion odds. Please assemble a one-page exec memo summarizing: ask, proposed structure (line items), unit-econ delta, and risks/mitigations. I will take the memo to the VP for commercial clearance and then CFO for final signoff.

Kim — if you can provide the delta and signoff language by EOD Monday I’ll escalate. Vivek — I’ll offer to the customer a conditional ‘in-principle’ acceptance pending executive signoff so they don’t stall.

Marissa
VP, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
To: Elena Park <elena@cardiosurge.health>
Cc: alex_martinez@redwood.com
Date: 2028-06-21T17:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot pricing ask (CardioSurge) — provisional terms and next steps

Elena — thanks for the patience. We can provide a provisional structure to unblock procurement: 35% off list for months 1-3, $50k onboarding credit issued as a rebate once month-3 usage reaches 80% of your projected baseline, and a 12-month renewal option with preferred committed pricing if you convert within 30 days. VPC deployment and SOC2 evidence are available; we’ll attach the audit pack to the DocuSign.

This is contingent on final VP/CFO signoff (internal memo in progress). If approved, we’ll issue a DocuSign with conditional rebate language and a 90-day validation/clawback clause. Can you confirm the projected month-3 usage threshold in the attached spreadsheet so we can finalize the contingency language?

Tentative next steps:
 - You confirm month-3 usage baseline in Q3_usage_projection_cardiosurge.xlsx
 - We circulate 1-page exec memo to VP/CFO (internal) by EOD Monday
 - Pending signoff, we’ll send DocuSign with conditional rebate and deployment SOW

If you prefer, we can set a 30-minute call tomorrow to go line-by-line.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
